BiblicalUsage: Misrephoth-maim is a place on the northern coast, the burnings of waters, named twice in the conquest. Joshua chased the northern kings as far as Misrephoth-maim, and God promised to drive out all who lived from Lebanon to Misrephoth-maim.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the name is a landmark of the promise: the land was given as far as the waters, and Joshua's victories ran to the very edge of it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
